terms.meaning: The Army, Navy and Air Force, which defend the country from attack.
Forces that support the defence forces in emergencies, such as the BSF and Coast Guard.
National Cadet Corps: training for school and college students; motto "Discipline and Unity".
Volunteers who help the police with internal security and in disasters.

items.name: Supreme Commander
items.formula: The President of India commands the defence forces.
items.example: The three services join the Independence Day and Republic Day parades.

items.name: India's borders
items.formula: 15,200 km of land border and 7,516.60 km of coast.
items.example: Duties: defend borders, keep the country united, stop smuggling.

items.name: Defence training centres
items.formula: National Defence College (New Delhi), Indian Military Academy (Dehra Dun), National Defence Academy (Khadakwasla, Pune).

items.name: The Indian Army
items.formula: Second largest in the world: 12,37,117 soldiers plus 9,60,000 reserves; led by a General.
items.example: It also does relief work in floods and earthquakes.

items.name: The Indian Navy
items.formula: Sixth largest in the world; led by an Admiral; aircraft carriers INS Virat and INS Vikramaditya.
items.example: The Seabird naval base is at Karwar.

items.name: The Indian Air Force
items.formula: Fourth largest in the world; led by an Air Chief Marshal; seven Commands.
items.example: About 1,00,000 personnel and 1330 war planes, including Jaguar and Rafale.

items.name: Headquarters of the services
items.formula: Army, Navy and Air Force headquarters are all in New Delhi.
items.example: Air Force training: Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Dindigul.

items.name: BSF and Border Roads
items.formula: BSF guards the borders (motto "Duty until Death") and fought at Kargil.
items.example: The Border Roads Organisation builds and clears roads and bridges.

items.name: Coast Guard and CISF
items.formula: The Coast Guard guards coasts, stops smuggling and rescues in storms.
items.example: The CISF (1,45,000 strong) is the world's largest industrial security force.

items.name: Indian Red Cross Society
items.formula: Works through branches in 1100 districts; the President of India is its President.

items.name: Army ranks, top down
items.formula: General, Lieutenant General, Major General, Brigadier, Colonel, Lieutenant Colonel, Major, Captain, Lieutenant.
items.example: Navy and Air Force have their own ranks.

mistakes.text: Army: second largest. Navy: sixth largest. Air Force: fourth largest.
Army chief: General. Navy chief: Admiral. Air Force chief: Air Chief Marshal.
"Duty until Death" is the BSF's motto; "Discipline and Unity" is the NCC's; "Serve Humanity" is the Red Cross's.
